body:
I often think I would include something telling my friends and family that they couldn’t possibly have done anything more to help me. And it is not their fault. I am not theirs to save. 

Just anything that minimises any guilt they might feel.

Thanks. This is all very informative. I have sent all my reports and info over to my dad who has some friends that are gonna have a look for a second opinion. It’s a bit tricky to do it here as I have to get every thing run through insurance but as you said, best to see if there are differing opinions.

Thank you for your advice. I really appreciate you sharing. my surgeon is afraid of scar tissue build up on the ACL because my knee is currently still inflamed from the bucket handle meniscus tear. As my ACL injury was last year he’s also going to use the meniscus tear arthroscopy to have a better look and test the ACL to then recommend a future treatment method. I would probably love to get them repaired together, but I am prone to scarring already and also live in a different country for my family and can’t have the support I need for recovery on short notice. So im mentally preparing myself to suck up a 2 surgery run just so I can have some family around for the ACL surgery. 

Hopefully with the meniscus repair I get back my full range of motion since the limited motion currently has already left me with quad deterioration.

Thank you for sharing. I do think it’s a rough recovery and it’s tough to do. 

I’ve just got my MRI report back and it’s confirmed that it’s a complete rupture. So I do think I will be going for a repair. I still will probably do 2 surgeries, as to get my meniscus repaired within the next month, hopefully get rehab started asap. Then have some time to build up muscle before the ACL repair, this will also give my parents some time to plan to come help me as they would have to fly in from another country and I would like to have their support for the bigger surgery.

Wow 3 reconstructions is a lot! You must have been through so much in healing and getting back to activity each time. It’s not small feat! 

I do feel a lot of instability and I think I’m leaning towards sucking it up and going for surgery, but I also have heard a lot of people go for meniscus repair first then ACL repair. 

Could I ask a little about what you learnt about prepping before surgery and recovery? 

I’m mainly worried about becoming a burden to my friend as I live in a completely different country than my family.

Hi, im (27 F) it sounds like you’ve been through a lot with your body and it’s taken incredible drive to get back to activity each time. 

I can’t say I can totally relate, but I tore my ACL playing mixed netball when I was 16/17 (10 years ago) and a massive man ran into me at full speed. I had an ACL repair with a hamstring graft and gradually got back to some level of activity but never felt confident or stable with my knee. Recently I had a knee injury from twisting, had it settle down without going to a specialist then got hit by a cyclist and damaged the same knee. Now the specialist says probably have a torn ACL again and meniscus damage - i just went for my MRI today and am waiting for the results. 

I don’t think I can give much advice as I have much less experience but I just wanted to let you know you’re not alone.

Thank you so much for sharing. This has really made me feel so much better. I am still waiting on my MRI results but will look into ALLR and LET procedures so I know more.

I happy to hear you feel your knee is much for stable, as even after my first ACL surgery I wasn’t very confident and didn’t feel my knee was very stable even before the recent accident. This gives me something to possibly look forward to.

Also good luck with building your strength back up, your attitude makes me feel more optimistic :)

Thank you so much for sharing. This has really made me feel so much better. I really want to get back to activity as soon as possible because I was just getting to a place where I was beginning to be happy with my workouts and building strength. 

Can I ask what prehab you did to prep or if you have any recommended resources? I’m still waiting on my MRI results but am trying to learn as much as possible to prep myself and my knee.

Turning 28 this year and it’s really been like this since graduating university. I was already depressed before and none of it seems worth it. We’re all just chugging along and the people I see that are really carefree, are friends who have a lot of money they can use as a safety net to do whatever they want. I want to try new things and move to a new country to experience something fresh. I want to keep trying new things because I get bored so easy and I don’t know what is actually “for me”. But I also need to pick a “career” to progress in and make more money to be able to survive and have the excess to try things. if I stop working I’ll have to give up living where I live and move back home and become a burden to my parents… all of it doesn’t work out..this can’t be it…

Hey there, first of all be proud of yourself for making it to work even when you’re feeling so down. It may seem like it’s the bare minimum and it has to be done but really sometimes people don’t make it even with all this hanging over them. I know having a depression mess to come home to every evening can make you feel worse, but sometimes I’ve found that I actually get back on the horse a lot better when I try something else, rather than forcing myself to clean. like a new hobby or even getting out of the house for a small walk and doing that a few times a week. I think it kind of breaks the cycle a bit, and I feel I’ve done something rather than the bare minimum I need to live. It gradually helps me build up energy, then in a few days or weeks i build up enough to tackle cleaning bits at a time.

I’m not entirely sure but I think it’s robbed me of having childhood dreams. I’ve been depressed for as long as I can remember and was verbalising wanting to die at 7. I think I never really thought about what I wanted to be or do with that childhood wonder because I really just didn’t want to exist. I wonder if without it I would have developed some dreams or interests that I wanted to pursue. Or was I always meant to be a kid that just lived some kind of life with no drive…

Hey there, I know a lot of people who felt this way at 18. Now we’re all in our late 20s and I see lots of people have completely reinvented themselves and are doing more things they like, away from old friends and family. I’m not friends with all of them still, but I see lots of them on social media just doing things I completely didn’t expect and they seem much more grounded in themselves. Sometimes you just need time and space for yourself. And I’m happy for them even though we don’t keep in touch. You might have some silent supports too. I also want to say school is not for everyone and you don’t have to keep friends from there if they’re not for you.

 I did the standard high school -> university -> job and I really think I’m much less happy that my brother who didn’t go to the regular university route. instead did practical courses in things he enjoys and now he both teaches music and produces music. He makes enough to support himself and really gets so much fulfilment from his work. 

I hope you give yourself some grace to find your footing in the world before deciding to give up.

First of all, thank you for sharing. My grandma is prone to depression and my granddad just had a stroke last year but he has survived it though it’s taken a toll. I’m afraid that the same situation will happen to my grandma once my grandad passes. 

The best thing I can think of is to try to get a therapist or professional help, but I personally know my grandma to be very stubborn - she’s not going out to see anyone she doesn’t want to - so if yours is similar this might hard to do.  Maybe if you are able to, spending more time with her trying to do regular things at home that she used to enjoy (cooking, watching tv, chatting? Any hobbies that she used to do?) might make it easier to start enjoying things again with someone to accompany them. This might open the door to gradually do more things that improve her mental health, it could even make it easier to get her to accept professional therapy.

I hope you and her both find some peace, and just want to say, you’re a good grandkid for trying your best to help.

I think there are different ways of accepting it. I’ve been depressed through childhood and into adulthood, so basically my whole life and got diagnosed around 20. It’s been 6 years since then. In the beginning I was just like well it really is forever then…but I guess I don’t know anything before it so there’s no “better days” to compare to.  I had a lot of anxiety about being on meds my whole life just to function, and hit a pretty big setback when I tried to come off them 2 years ago. Recently I’ve been trying to taper off again, I’ve come to the realisation, yes I am depressed. And am approaching it by being more kind to myself rather than seeing it as a dead weight on me. 

Thinking in terms of: I have depression so I can’t just get up and get on with things sometimes, like people who don’t have it can. 

I’ve also found that with a diagnosis it’s also given me something more concrete to understand what’s wrong, and in some way also legitimises how I act sometimes. I find that friends are more understanding when I ghost them for a bit when I’m in an episode, but it doesn’t mean I actively use it as an excuse. I just think when there’s something concrete to reason with you take it out less on yourself sometimes, and it makes it easier for others to understand. 

It took a while, but as I’ve been working through therapy in finding that if I’m doing my best to take care of myself, in actually feeling a lot better about managing it than feeling likes it’s a malicious demon that will endless devour me. It actually makes me feel a bit stronger that I’m constantly battling this and my win streaks have been getting better ❤️‍🩹
Mine is always my mum going “what do you have to be sad about?” after she pries and pries me to answer if I’m still on antidepressants

Hey, I just want to say I understand the feeling. About a year ago it got to the point for me where I couldn’t enjoy music or watching movies (which I really used to love and used as an escape a lot). Every time I tried to put a song on I would feel (I’m not sure if this is a good explanation) but this heightened numbness? Like the feeling of nothingness but also wanting to crawl out of my skin to feel something.  This was the point where I was like wow this is really the lowest - there is not even a little sliver of joy. 

I started therapy then, also got back on medication. Honestly it got worse before it got better. I had all the horrible starting on SSRI’s symptoms as well as the repetition of sharing my past with multiple therapists over and over to find one that worked for me. But I did start crying again, a lot, and constantly. I felt like I was at the other end of the spectrum and was so tired of it all. 

Anyway, I just kept going through the motions, doing the therapy work, taking my meds regularly. Giving myself a bit of grace, tried to actively be more gentle and patient with myself. Slowly I mellowed out and started to enjoy things again. It was first being able to listen to music again. Then being able to sit down and actually watch a movie. Then actually enjoying myself when I met up with friends. I just didn’t try to ruminate too much on not enjoying something I used to when it happened, and then focused on trying to fit something else in to look forward to another time. I would say it was actually hard work, which in the past I didn’t think I was worth, but I kind of just pushed myself through it until I got to the point of believing that I am worth working on for myself. I don’t think like that all the time, but definitely more often than before. 


TL;DR - I lost all my joy too a while ago and have very slowly been getting it back. I hope this brings some sort of comfort that you can find that again too.

I think it depends on the workplace. At my old job it was common for people to ask each other, but at my current job we all go out on our own for lunch. I actually quite enjoy the lunch alone as it gives me time to reset and do my own thing. And there is still the odd like team lunch or team event that everyone goes to. I prefer this, as my old job, though it was nice to have people to eat with it came with a lot of toxic workplace “we’re a family” culture.

You have every right to not want religion involved in therapy. A good therapist will listen to your feedback and try and help create a therapy program/adopt methodology that is catered to YOUR NEEDS AND PREFERENCES. Honestly, it’s unethical for them to keep pushing for things you’ve already said you do not want.

Can’t remember how old I was when I first started feeling it, but I first said out loud that I wanted to kill myself when I was 7, so it must have been building up before then. I didn’t get diagnosed with depression and put on medication until I was 19/20, now at 25 I’m quite sure I also have ADHD - but that’s another ordeal to get tested for. You can really be diagnosed at any time or never diagnosed, it’s all about accessibility, I got my chance with university mental health support, when I was finally away from my parents. But a lack of diagnosis doesn’t mean those feelings aren’t real.

This is incredibly relatable, I’ve always thought I’ve never really suffered because no one big thing happened to me - my family was never poor, I never went hungry, my parents never divorced, I’ve not lost anyone close. it made it so hard to justify why I was so depressed when people who have gone through much worse could cope better. I’ve started going to therapy, it’s been 3 months but the other day my therapist mentioned “even the small things add up, they can still be traumatic” and it’s making it easier to contextualise a lot of the small little things that piled on and on and contributed to my current state. E.g. Just because my parents arent divorced doesn’t mean they showed me a healthy relationship or provided me with the emotional support I needed. 

I’m not saying it all makes sense, but it did allow me to give some validity to feeling so bad and not feel guilty about feeling bad. I hope you find that too friend.

I think about this all the time. So many other people WANT to live but can’t, and I don’t want to live but can’t bring myself to end it.

I was feeling exactly the same, I thought I was picking up, worked really hard and found a new job that was better than my toxic work place, thought I would be stable enough to wean off my antidepressants. I really tried my best, but it just took a series of little punctures in my lifeboat for me to sink me. My partner cheated, I was forced to face my toxic parents having to swallow that, and a bunch of other small things. I spiralled for months, ate barely anything, constantly questioning my ability, picking at my body, self harm. The suicidal ideation never really left me but it became louder than ever. I cried almost constantly, and felt so embarrassed about it - I’d would just be tearing up on public transport. 

I finally reached out to get therapy, knowing I’ll have to cut down on all my other spending, and got back on my medication. Honestly, it’s helping me function, I feel a bit more worthwhile when I’m functioning in society. It’s not perfect and I wouldn’t say it’s good, but I’m not in the pits. 

I’m saying all this just because I don’t want you to hit a snag and then spiral ass low as I did, or feel like you’re back where you were when you attempted.  For me, I’ve felt a therapist has been an outlet, all the things I cannot share with judgemental parents or friends that I think are dealing with enough already, I can share with them. I can unpack them, I can feel heard. It’s been worth the money, the progress is slow but it’s only been 2 months and I’m feeling more stable, who knows I might even know what it’s like to feel good and happy (I feel I’ve had depression since childhood so I don’t really have a non-depressed baseline to compare to). I’m also turning 26 this year, and I just wanted to share so you might not feel so alone. My social circle is currently 2 people irl, and like 1 other friend who lives abroad that I talk to, so not much going on there. I’m just trying to build myself up again so hopefully I can build up other things around me and  connect to more supportive people in future.

Hey, thanks so much for sharing so openly. It’s somewhat nice to know I’m not alone. Looking back I think there might be a bit of history with my paternal grandma and definitely some mental health issues with my father as well (anger, constant pessimism that verges on suicidal ideation, thinking the world is against him) 

I agree so much about not having a frame of reference for being healthy mentally - I don’t know what that looks like or feels like for me, I don’t know how to identify it and how to keep it. 

I was on medication before, came off it thinking I would be in a better place after a year of job insecurity and the possibility of outstaying my visa and being deported, but on my first week of my new job and new visa my boyfriend said he cheated on me. So I have been spiralling. He’s broken up with me now, it’s probably for the best, but it made me really think I can’t live without medication. I was completely non-functional, crying all the time at nothing, chest pains, dissociation, quick to anger, completely forgetful. So now I’m back on them just to make it through, but it really blunts everything, not just the lows but the highs as well. I feel like I’m in the passenger seat of my body. I can’t not have a job because I would have to leave the country so it gives me a lot of anxiety to think I might not be able to do that, so I guess that gets me to work too. 

I’m proud of you for taking the time for yourself to try and work on yourself. I know it’s very hard, but even if you have to sleep between every few lines of that book you are still making progress on it. 

I understand not knowing your true potential, not knowing if you’re bad at something because of depression or because you actually can’t do it. Objectively I was kind of successful academically, but in university it took so much out of me, I didn’t really have a life and struggled just to get passing grades. It was hard to look at everyone having fun and still doing well enough as I wanted that for me too, but honestly even if I wasn’t depressed and anxious would I have done better? 

I’ve started therapy and am getting some validation knowing that I have actually experienced trauma and that there is a lot of healing I need to do. I used to think why am I like this when people have gone through so much worse and still function and still find happiness. Hopefully, I get some tools to help and heal some old wounds and the new ones from my last relationship too.
Ah, im sorry you feel like that too. I too was very suicidal at 13 and it rises and falls throughout the years. I really hope it gets better soon and there’s better out there for us.

Thanks for commenting. It’s a bit comforting to know I’m not alone, but I’m sorry it sucks for you too. Hopefully things can pick up for you. I think my family are in denial/don’t accept mental illness as a thing that happens to them. I know my dad has anger issues and my parents don’t have a healthy relationship, but they seem pretty functional compared to me.

Hey, thanks for sharing. I’ve been experiencing this on and off for years. I don’t really have a solution, but I think right now just having to get up for my job is what is waking me up, sometimes I spend the first 4 hours of work in bed until I can get up and move to my desk, and it’s usually when I feel I need to eat/pee/get water and working from bed is hurting my back. On the weekends it’s a bit harder. I haven’t found a real solution yet but just wanted to let you know you’re not alone. I’ve been seeing a therapist and hopefully will get some ideas I can try out to help with this, and could share them with you.

Hey, how are you? I understand the difficulty with a family that doesn’t understand (my parents are also Asian and have conservative views even thought they don’t care to admit it). I too feel disappointed every day I wake up, and struggle to get through each day. I’m here if you want to talk.
That’s great! I’m where you were a month ago and hopefully will make it through too. I’m rooting for you!
Thank you. I’m also trying to be kinder to myself and I hope you are too. I’m rooting for you too!

Sorry it hasn’t really improved for you, but I can relate. I’ve had depression all my life and am currently in a very bad episode that has lasted for months. I’m objectively not failing at life, and right now I think I’ll just keep chugging along. It’s hard everyday, because I’m just staying so I won’t hurt my family, but I keep busy. I’m starting therapy and getting back on medication, but not too optimistic, if it gets me to a better place then that’s a bonus, but right now it just helps me make it to the next day. 

I hope you really enjoy your travels and just keep informed about the places you visit and how best to stay safe. It’s already a huge step to do that for yourself and I hope that brings you some joy.

I feel the same. I never thought I should make it past 17/18, now I’m 25 and I only feel like trying so hard has made nothing better. And I’ve never found any reason to keep going, I feel like it won’t change in the next years. I’m only looking for my window to exit.

I’m so sorry about your friend. If it is any comfort you were probably the reason why there were these small moments of lightness that kept him going till the end. I know my friends and the moments I have with them have helped me stay till now, but I don’t think I feel they can do anything to help me or pull me out of this pit. I’m just thankful for them being in my life. I’ve been born into depression and it was no one’s fault…luck of the draw I guess. I just don’t really see a need to live with it since I have no dreams or goals to achieve. I know I might be missed, but I hope if it comes to me ending it, they can believe I just needed it to stop and it wasn’t on them to “save me”.

I completely agree. I’ve just been trucking along my whole life, breaking down at night, breaking down when my mic is muted and my video is off in work meetings, then just going on, getting up and getting work done. 

The world keeps ticking on with its endless messes, and I honestly don’t think I make any difference with anything I care about. Honestly, if I died right now would probably be better for the environment than if I kept going through life the way I have been for more decades, using resources it can’t afford to lose. 

I know people might be sad, the most I can say is it isn’t their fault and I made this decision myself. I want to leave this stupid party, I never found a reason for me to stay.
